Do you want to help leading Nordic banks, insurers and capital markets firms shape their future, navigate complex business challenges, and translate strategic ambitions into tangible business results?

jobs.occupation: PhD scholarship in applied microbial dynamics for tropical farm fermentations - BRIGHT
jobs.description:
Are you interested in microbial ecology and food fermentation, and at the same time eager to work towards more sustainable food systems? Then join us as our new PhD Student in tropical farm fermentations

The overwhelming majority of coffee and cocoa are produced in the tropics, and represent vast economic drivers globally as these products continue to transform from commodities to luxury goods. Alongside other factors, the quality of these goods is largely influenced by post-harvest processing, which modulates microbial activity, in turn leading to differences in sensory impact. Complex microbial dynamics affect fermentation outcomes and sensory attributes, and understanding these dynamics and how relevant microbial consortia can be mobilised to modulate these outcomes pose challenging questions that can lead to multiple applications, including ones with health implications. This project aims to unravel some of the underlying microbial dynamics of tropical fermentations such as coffee, cocoa, or other traditional tropical fermentation, utilizing a combination of metagenomics, strain characterization, and solid-state fermentation.

This position is part of a wider cross-institutional research programme on “Microbial fermentation innovations for a resilient food system, optimised human health and environmental sustainability”. You will be working at the interface of biotechnology, genetics, and fermentation in a cutting-edge interdisciplinary and multi-cultural research environment, and will have the opportunity to go on research stay (one-year minimum, preferably two) with our partner institution the Biotransformation & Engineering (BTE) department at the Singapore Institute of Food and Biotechnology Innovation (SIFBI) under the Agency for Science, Research and Technology (A*STAR) in Singapore.

The job
As our PhD student in tropical farm fermentations, you will:

• Analyse metagenomic profiles of artisanal tropical fermentations
• Characterise extant yeast and bacteria for relevant traits for fermentative capability and other functional capacities
• Perform solid state fermentations in controlled settings to achieve targeted outcomes
• Evaluate fermentations via microbiology, molecular biology, and analytic chemistry
• Validate effects of post-fermentation processing on physicochemical qualities and aroma profiles
• Explore potential environmental and socio-economic ramifications of luxury commodities from tropical farm fermentations
What we’re looking for
You will have a two-year Master’s degree (120 ECTS points) in molecular biology, genetics, biotechnology, microbiology, or closely related disciplines, or a similar degree with an academic level equivalent to a two-year Master's degree.

You will have excellent organizational and project management skills and enjoy developing new methods.

You will be fluent in spoken and written English and have literacy in common IT systems

The ideal candidate will also:

• have experience with molecular biology techniques and, ideally, some foundational understanding in metagenomics, microbial ecology, microbiology, analytical chemistry and/or sensory science
• have a genuine interest in food systems and sustainability
• be able to work with others and independently, and adaptable to working in multi-cultural environments
• be comfortable in an interdisciplinary environment, and a willingness to bridge microbial biotechnology with food and sensory science
• be patient, charitable, curious and playful—key qualities for interdisciplinary work
Approval and Enrolment 
The scholarship for the PhD degree is subject to academic approval, and the candidate will be enrolled in one of the general degree programmes at DTU. For information about our enrolment requirements and the general planning of the PhD study programme, please see DTU's rules for the PhD education. 

Assessment
The assessment of the applicants will be made by co-supervisors, Dr. Tiffany Mak and Dr. Eric Peterson, and primary supervisor, Prof. Morten Sommer.

We offer
DTU is a leading technical university globally recognized for the excellence of its research, education, innovation and scientific advice. We offer a rewarding and challenging job in an international environment. We strive for academic excellence in an environment characterized by collegial respect and academic freedom tempered by responsibility.

Salary and appointment terms
The appointment will be based on the collective agreement with the Danish Confederation of Professional Associations. Please see DTU’s salary structure for scientific staff: www.inside.dtu.dk/en/human-resources/during-employment/salary/salary-structures

The period of employment is 3 years, full time. 

Start date is 01-04-2027 or according to mutual agreement. 

You can read more about career paths at DTU here.

Further information
For additional information about the position, please contact Researcher Tiffany Mak at tifmak@dtu.dk, or Senor Scientist Eric Peterson at Eric_Peterson@a-star.edu.sg. 

You can read more about BRIGHT below, and at www.bright.dtu.dk 

If you are applying from abroad, you may find useful information on working in Denmark and at DTU at DTU – Moving to Denmark. Furthermore, you have the option of joining our monthly free seminar “PhD relocation to Denmark and startup “Zoom” seminar” for all questions regarding the practical matters of moving to Denmark and working as a PhD at DTU. 

Application procedure 
Your complete online application must be submitted no later than 15 December 2026 (23:59 Danish time). 

Applications must be submitted as one PDF file containing all materials to be given consideration. To apply, please open the link "Apply now", fill out the online application form, and attach all your materials in English in one PDF file. The file must include:

• A letter motivating the application (cover letter)
• Curriculum vitae 
• Grade transcripts and BSc/MSc diploma (in English) including official description of grading scale
• One letter of reference, with referee’s email and phone number
Candidates will be invited to the first round of interviews between 7-11 January 2027.

You may apply prior to obtaining your master's degree but cannot begin before having received it.

Applications received after the deadline will not be considered.

All interested candidates irrespective of age, gender, disability, race, religion or ethnic background are encouraged to apply. As DTU works with research in critical technology, which is subject to special rules for security and export control, open-source background checks may be conducted on qualified candidates for the position.

Microbial Foods Group
The Microbial Foods Group is focused on exploring fundamental microbial processes within our food system from a planetary health perspective. We are committed to addressing pressing global food systems and sustainability challenges through integrated and multi-scalar approaches. A key goal is to understand and develop microbially-driven processes that can be effectively implemented to substantially reduce the environmental impact of our current food production system.

BRIGHT – The Novo Nordisk Foundation Biotechnology Research Institute for the Green Transition
The Novo Nordisk Foundation Biotechnology Research Institute for the Green Transition (BRIGHT) is a major initiative based at DTU that aims to accelerate the development of biosolutions and strengthen the bio-based economy. BRIGHT serves as a hub for academic and industrial partners working together to unlock the potential of bioproduction. BRIGHT focuses on three main areas: Sustainable materials (Developing bio-based alternatives to fossil-derived materials), Microbial foods (Innovating food production through microbial technologies), and Microorganisms for net-zero agriculture (Creating solutions to reduce greenhouse gas emissions in agriculture). The goal is to develop and scale innovative biosolutions within these areas, ultimately creating sustainable and competitive alternatives to fossil-based products and processes that can make significant contributions to reducing global greenhouse gas emissions.

jobs.description:
Are you curious about the diverse microbial interactions in fermentation, whilst eager to contribute towards more sustainable food systems? Then join us as our new PhD Student in microbial consortia for solid-state fermentation! 

Existing microbial food productions have largely focused on liquid state fermentation as the main production strategy under industrial settings. This approach however limits the media composition, excluding the potential use of substrates with lower solubility, as well as substrates mixtures that are heterogeneous by nature. Additionally, there are notable environmental impacts of large-scale liquid state fermenters, especially in terms of freshwater use, both during the fermentation process, as well as downstream purification steps. Furthermore, many existing fermentation approaches rely on pure isolates of microbial starter cultures, which limits the potential functional benefits when compared to mixed microbial communities, both in terms of the functional qualities (including taste, texture and nutrition) of the final product, as well as the safety and robustness of the fermentation process.

This project therefore seeks to address some of these limitations by exploring the potential of using microbial consortia for solid-state fermentation (SSF) in microbial foods production. A key focus will be on identifying and characterising promising fungal-bacterial interactions in mixed microbial consortia, and evaluating their respective influences on different fermentation outcomes and functional qualities, with a focus on the nutritional composition and other potential human health modulating factors of the final microbial food. 

This position is part of a wider cross-institutional research programme on “Microbial fermentation innovations for a resilient food system, optimised human health and environmental sustainability”. You will be working at the interface of biotechnology, genetics, and fermentation in a cutting-edge interdisciplinary and multi-cultural research environment, and will have the opportunity to go on research stay (one-year minimum) with our partner institution at the Department of Food Science & Technology at the National University of Singapore (NUS) under the Agency for Science, Research and Technology (A*STAR) in Singapore.

The job
As our PhD student in microbial consortia for solid-state fermentation, you will:

• Conduct metagenomic profiling on selected microbial foods to identify potential interacting microbial species for experimental validation
• Develop combinatorial screening methods on selective microbial and substrate combinations based on specified functional characteristics, and establish optimised solid state fermentation parameters
• Characterise the nutritional and related functional properties, including in vitro digestibility and in vitro gut microbiome modulation, of the fermented microbial foods using multi-omic approaches
• Develop genome-scale metabolic models for selective mixed microbial communities and experimentally validate their predictive outcomes

You will have a two-year Master’s degree (120 ECTS points) in molecular biology, genetics, biotechnology, microbiology, or closely related disciplines, or a similar degree with an academic level equivalent to a two-year Master's degree.

You will have excellent organizational and project management skills and enjoy developing new methods.

• have a keen interest in food sustainability, nutrition and planetary health
• be able to work with others and independently, and adaptable to working in multi-cultural environments

jobs.occupation: Postdoctoral position in probabilistic inversion of seismic data for mapping submerged landscapes and archaeological potential
jobs.description:
The Department of Geoscience, Aarhus University, Denmark, invites applications for a postdoctoral position in probabilistic inversion of seismic data, with the aim of identifying submerged landscapes and locations of archaeological potential. We are searching for a motivated and engaged researcher with experience in inversion to be part of our research team studying late Quaternary and Holocene processes and landscape evolution.

The postdoctoral position is a fixed-term full-time position for 1 year.

The postdoctoral work will be part of the international ERC Synergy Grant project SUBNORDICA, where scientists in the fields of geology, geophysics, and archaeology work together to develop methodologies for recreating submerged landscapes and human settlement in NW Europe, and for finding submerged Stone Age settlements in deeper water settings such as the North Sea. SUBNORDICA also uses machine-learning routines to identify, from existing and new data, targets of archaeological potential for more detailed investigation. The research team at the department is leading a work package focused on the eastern North Sea region. Other members in the team work on geophysical imaging methods, sea level modelling, and palaeolandscape mapping to generate palaeotopography and palaeocoastlines using both legacy and newly acquired data.

Job description
The postdoctoral position is focused on probabilistic inversion of seismic data to estimate subsurface properties that can be linked directly to the location of submerged settlements – a key example being the presence of peat, which marks former dry land.

Specific tasks will be to:

• Develop probabilistic inversion workflows for high-resolution subbottom profiles and multichannel seismic data from the North Sea, constrained by sediment core observations
• Map peat and other landscape types relevant for archaeology, and use the results together with machine-learning routines to identify targets of archaeological potential
• Provide input and constraints for predictive modelling workflows carried out at partner institutions
The postdoctoral researcher will be working closely together with post docs and senior staff in the research team at the department, as well as with the international partners in the SUBNORDICA project. Close collaboration is expected particularly with partners focused on predictive modelling for archaeology. The position provides opportunities for offshore field work and participation in joint research expeditions in the North Sea and Baltic Sea. It is also expected that the postdoc will take an active part in various research team activities and contribute to supervision and teaching of (under-) graduate students in the team.

Facilities
Laboratory facilities at the Department of Geoscience will be available for the position. This includes the acquisition, processing and interpretation facilities at SeisLab Aarhus for both multi- and single channel marine seismic and acoustic data, and an advanced sediment core laboratory.

Qualifications
The qualified applicant will have a PhD degree in geoscience, geophysics or related fields. Candidates should preferably have a background within probabilistic inversion and uncertainty quantification and/or machine learning. Experience with seismic data, including reflection seismic and hydroacoustic data, is beneficial, as is experience with linking seismic data to physical or lithological properties. Experience with the shallow subsurface of the North Sea or other similar settings, including sediment cores and marine geoarchaeology, is further beneficial but not required.

The candidate is expected to have well-documented research experience with academic publications and presentations at conferences and meetings. The applicant should also have effective organizational skills, with previous project management being beneficial. The candidate should be able to work collaboratively as part of an interdisciplinary team of geophysicists, geologists and archaeologists. Oral and written English skills are required.

Application
The application must include the following:

• Cover Letter, including motivation for applying and information on how the candidate’s qualifications and experience will aid the project
• Curriculum Vitae, including a list of publications
• PhD certificate or a statement regarding the expected date of completing of PhD studies
• One page statement of research goals
• Contact information (name, position, institution, email) for three references
We refer to the faculty’s guidelines for applicants.

Aarhus University’s goal is to be an attractive and inspiring workplace for all and to build a culture in which each employee has opportunities to thrive, advance and develop. We view equality and diversity as assets, and we welcome all applicants.

Place and conditions of employment
Your place of work would be the Department of Geoscience, Høegh-Guldbergs Gade 2, DK-8000 Aarhus C, Denmark.

The Department of Geoscience prioritizes diversity and a good work environment, as this is a prerequisite for conducting progressive research. At the department, we have a diverse and international research environment, with skilled employees and access to modern and well-equipped laboratories.

Contact information
Professor Katrine Juul Andresen (katrine.andresen@geo.au.dk)

Associate Professor Thomas Mejer Hansen (tmeha@geo.au.dk)

Application procedure

This means that after the deadline for applications – and with the assistance from the assessment committee chairman, and the appointment committee if necessary, – the head of department selects the candidates to be evaluated. All applicants will be notified whether or not their applications have been sent to an expert assessment committee for evaluation. The selected applicants will be informed about the composition of the committee, and each applicant is given the opportunity to comment on the part of the assessment that concerns him/her self. 

Formalities and salary range
Natural Sciences refers to the Ministerial Order on the Appointment of Academic Staff at Danish Universities under the Danish Ministry of Science, Technology and Innovation.

The application must be in English and include a curriculum vitae, degree certificate, a complete list of publications, a statement of future research plans and information about research activities, teaching portfolio and verified information on previous teaching experience (if any). Guidelines for applicants can be found here.

Appointment shall be in accordance with the collective labour agreement between the Danish Ministry of Taxation and the Danish Confederation of Professional Associations. Salary and terms as agreed between the Danish Ministry of Taxation and the Confederation of Professional Unions at basic salary steps 4-8.

JOB DESCRIPTION

At Genmab, we are dedicated to building extra[not]ordinary® futures, together, by developing antibody products and groundbreaking, knock-your-socks-off KYSO antibody medicines® that change lives and the future of cancer treatment and serious diseases. We strive to create, champion and maintain a global workplace where individuals’ unique contributions are valued and drive innovative solutions to meet the needs of our patients, care partners, families and employees.

Our people are compassionate, candid, and purposeful, and our business is innovative and rooted in science. We believe that being proudly authentic and determined to be our best is essential to fulfilling our purpose. Yes, our work is incredibly serious and impactful, but we have big ambitions, bring a ton of care to pursuing them, and have a lot of fun while doing so.

Does this inspire you and feel like a fit? Then we would love to have you join us!

The Role

Genmab is looking for a dedicated Manager to take responsibility for GMP equipment qualification and validation at our new manual clinical secondary packaging and labelling facility in Ballerup.

You will be part of a small, agile team supporting clinical trials, helping ensure that high-quality investigational medicinal products reach patients globally with cancer and other serious diseases on time and in full.

As Genmab’s newly established in-house GMP production capability for secondary packaging and labelling, the facility offers a unique opportunity to help establish equipment, processes and ways of working from the beginning. You will play a key role in ensuring that equipment is fit for its intended use, appropriately qualified and maintained in a qualified state throughout its lifecycle.

This is a position with responsibility for leading activities and coordinating stakeholders within your area of expertise. The role does not include line management or direct reports.

The position is based at our Ballerup site and requires on-site presence. You will report to the Associate Director, Team Lead, Global Clinical Supply, based in Ballerup.

Responsibilities

The role combines technical ownership, hands-on qualification activities, GMP documentation and hands-on production work in our manual packaging and labelling operations. Working closely with colleagues in Global Clinical Supply, operations, Quality Assurance, Facility and external suppliers, you will drive activities from defining requirements and planning qualifications through execution, reporting and ongoing lifecycle management.

• Own and coordinate qualification and validation activities for GMP equipment supporting clinical packaging, labelling and storage, ensuring that scope, documentation and testing reflect intended use and identified risks.

• Develop and maintain qualification strategies, plans, risk assessments, User Requirements Specifications and qualification documentation, including protocols and reports for Design, Installation, Operational and Performance Qualification, as applicable.

• Coordinate supplier deliverables and review technical documentation to ensure that equipment and supporting documentation meet defined requirements.

• Take responsibility for temperature mapping and qualification of temperature-controlled storage equipment, including associated monitoring and alarm functions, in collaboration with relevant stakeholders.

• Establish and maintain the qualified state of equipment through periodic reviews, requalification and assessment of changes, maintenance and calibration activities.

• Lead investigations and resolution of deviations arising during qualification and validation and manage related change controls and CAPAs in collaboration with Quality Assurance and equipment users.

• Develop and maintain SOPs, work instructions and equipment lifecycle documentation, ensuring clear responsibilities and practical, compliant routines.

• Contribute to inspection and audit readiness by maintaining complete, traceable documentation and presenting activities within your area of responsibility.

• Drive practical improvements that strengthen equipment reliability, documentation quality and efficient execution of qualification and validation activities.

• Perform hands-on secondary packaging and labelling activities for clinical trials in accordance with approved procedures, batch documentation and GMP, including manual set-up and operation, in-process checks, reconciliation of materials and labels, and timely, accurate completion of batch documentation and logbooks.

As part of a small team, you will also participate in day-to-day secondary packaging and labelling activities for clinical trials. This is an expected part of the role, with the balance between qualification activities and production work varying according to operational needs. Flexibility and a willingness to contribute across tasks are essential to ensuring timely clinical supplies.

Qualifications

• A relevant degree in engineering, pharmaceutical sciences, natural sciences or a related technical field, or equivalent qualifications supported by substantial relevant experience.

• Five or more years of relevant experience in a GMP-regulated environment, including independent responsibility for equipment qualification and validation.

• Demonstrated experience planning, documenting and executing qualification activities, including risk assessments, requirements specifications, test protocols and reports.

• A solid understanding of GMP requirements, equipment lifecycle principles, data integrity and risk-based qualification approaches.

• Experience with deviations, change controls, CAPAs and technical investigations.

• Ability to translate technical and operational requirements into clear, testable acceptance criteria and robust documentation.

• Experience working with equipment suppliers and coordinating activities across operations and Quality Assurance.

• Experience with packaging and labelling equipment e.g. Label printers, refrigerators, temperature-controlled storage or monitoring systems is an advantage.

• Experience establishing new equipment or working in a facility start-up environment is considered a plus.

• Hands-on experience with GMP production, ideally secondary packaging and labelling, is an advantage, together with a willingness to complete the training required to perform these activities.

• Proficient in English (written and spoken); Danish is an advantage.

• Good IT skills and willingness to learn new digital tools and systems.

About You

You are a structured and technically curious professional who enjoys taking ownership from initial requirements to completed qualifications and ongoing operation. You combine attention to detail with sound judgment and a practical approach to solving problems.

You are comfortable leading activities through your expertise, building alignment across functions and following up on commitments. You communicate clearly, challenge assumptions constructively and ensure that decisions and conclusions are supported by appropriate documentation.

You thrive in a small team where collaboration and flexibility are essential. You enjoy working close to equipment and operations, and you are motivated by building reliable, practical ways of working in an evolving environment. You can balance changing priorities while maintaining a clear focus on quality, compliance and patient needs.

The Team

You will be part of Global Clinical Supply Manufacturing, joining a highly competent team focused on GMP applicable to packaging and labelling of supplies for clinical trials, with a strong focus on quality, inspection readiness and successful collaboration with our internal stakeholders and CMOs.

Together with Global Clinical Supply Portfolio & Project Delivery and Global Clinical Supply Systems, the teams make up the Global Clinical Supply department.

We have an international and informal working environment with a high pace, strong one-team spirit and close collaboration across functions.

Application

If this opportunity excites you, please upload your CV and a short cover letter explaining your motivation for the role. Applications are reviewed on an ongoing basis, and interviews will be scheduled accordingly.

The proposed gross annual/hourly base salary range for this position, in the primary location, based on a full time schedule is:

DKK584.000,00---876.000,00

The final salary offer will depend on several factors, including your skills, qualifications, and experience.

In addition to base salary, this position is eligible for additional forms of compensation, such as discretionary bonuses and long-term incentives.

When you join Genmab, you become a part of a culture that supports your physical, financial, social, and emotional well-being. Our benefits include, but are not limited to:

• Pension

• Health insurance and wellness benefits

• Paid time off

• Employee support programs

Further details on eligibility for compensation and benefits based on the role will be provided during the recruitment process.

About Genmab

Genmab is an international biotechnology company with a core purpose to improve the lives of patients through innovative and differentiated antibody therapeutics. For 25 years, its hard-working, innovative and collaborative team has invented next-generation antibody technology platforms and harnessed translational, quantitative and data sciences, resulting in a proprietary pipeline including bispecific T-cell engagers, antibody-drug conjugates, next-generation immune checkpoint modulators and effector function-enhanced antibodies. By 2030, Genmab’s vision is to transform the lives of people with cancer and other serious diseases with Knock-Your-Socks-Off (KYSO®) antibody medicines.

Established in 1999, Genmab is headquartered in Copenhagen, Denmark with international presence across North America, Europe and Asia Pacific. For more information, please visit Genmab.com and follow us on LinkedIn and X.
